text:
Generally, all Israeli citizens are eligible for a passport, unless they did not live in Israel for 36 months out of the 5 years after acquiring citizenship. 

If you moved abroad two years after getting citizenship, you may not be eligible for a normal passport. But if this is the case, then you will still be given a red Teudat Maavar (Travel Document in Lieu of a National Passport). This is like a passport - you can use it to travel to Israel and elsewhere, but some countries will require that you get a visa. (Other countries will treat it the same as an Israeli passport - such as most EU countries, I understand) :) 

If you want to clarify your eligibility, you can probably contact the Consulate in Vancouver. But otherwise, I think is a pretty clear policy - I'm not sure it's something that a lawyer can necessarily help you get around.
